name: json.h
baseline: nlohmann/json (C++11, v2.0.3 as pinned by nativejson-benchmark); the same table also has JsonCpp 1.0.0, Jansson and cJSON
workload: Parse of canada.json, citm_catalog.json and twitter.json from an in-memory buffer into a DOM, time in ms; the harness adds an atof() pass over every number for json.h because json.h keeps numbers as strings.
claimed_speedup: Parse time in ms, json.h vs nlohmann: canada.json 9.418 vs 55.591 (5.9x), citm_catalog.json 5.077 vs 9.875 (1.9x), twitter.json 2.351 vs 7.010 (3.0x); three-file total 16.846 vs 72.476 ms (4.3x) (ratios derived from page data). Also parses faster than JsonCpp (142.458 / 14.587 / 8.477 ms), Jansson (78.465 / 22.656 / 10.935 ms) and cJSON (15.574 / 5.580 / 3.517 ms). Stringify canada.json 29.355 vs 76.315 ms. RapidJSON is still faster than json.h (4.755 / 1.950 / 1.227 ms parse).
compiler_and_flags: clang 7.0 (named in the result file name); premake5 release configuration uses optimize "Full" plus -march=native (build/premake5.lua)
hardware: Intel Core i7-4980HQ @ 2.80GHz, macOS 64-bit build (from the result file name 'Corei7-4980HQ@2.80GHz_mac64_clang7.0')
tradeoffs: Read-only DOM in one allocation (2 allocations in the benchmark), non-streaming, numbers kept as unparsed strings so callers convert them. Memory is large on number-heavy input: canada.json 18,010,128 bytes vs nlohmann 5,293,488 (3.4x, derived from page data). The same suite's conformance table records 9 failed parse-validation cases and 7 of 9 failed string-parse cases for json.h (nlohmann passes all of both), so it accepts some invalid JSON and does not decode some string escapes in that vendored version.
caveats: Numbers are the project-independent nativejson-benchmark sample run (README says update on 2016-9-9) on a 2014-era CPU with clang 7.0, an old vendored json.h and nlohmann v2.0.3; nlohmann/json has been reworked since, and json.h has since added fixes (commits 2026-10-02 reject raw control characters in quoted strings, 2026-10-06 comment handling) so the measured parser was more permissive and the ratios may differ today. The json.h README itself makes no speed claim and links no benchmark; the win is a derived comparison between rows of a third-party shootout (the suite author also wrote RapidJSON). The harness number post-pass uses atof, which is not full-precision parsing. Public-domain dedication, no patent grant. Flags and CPU come from the premake file and result file name, not from a prose methodology section.

name: libdart
baseline: nlohmann/json (version not stated); the same run also has RapidJSON, sajson, YAJL and Jansson
workload: Google Benchmark run over the repo's benchmark/input.json (newline-separated JSON packets): parse each packet to a DOM, key lookups on the parsed result, and serialize back to a string.
claimed_speedup: Single-run table, ns per pass over the input: Dart finalized parse 27682 vs nlohmann 254695 (9.2x), Dart dynamic parse 158967 vs nlohmann 254695 (1.6x), Dart key lookups 3803 vs 8471 (2.2x), Dart finalized serialize 36241 vs nlohmann 68175 (1.9x), Dart dynamic serialize 43105 vs 68175 (1.6x) (ratios derived from page data). sajson parses faster than Dart (14360 ns) and RapidJSON in-situ is close (34035 ns). PARSING.md: Dart runs 'within about 50% of RapidJSON' on parse.
hardware: 'middle-end 2018 MacBook Pro'; Google Benchmark header reports 8 X 2300 MHz CPUs, L3 6291K; exact CPU model not named
tradeoffs: Object keys are stored lexicographically sorted (iteration order is stable but not insertion order); no incremental parsing; finalized packets are immutable flat buffers, mutation needs a dynamic heap form and an expensive lowering step; copy-on-write reference counting (thread-unsafe pointer used in the benchmark). Header-only C++14 interface plus an ABI-stable C89 interface. JSON parsing itself is delegated to RapidJSON or sajson, YAML to libyaml.
caveats: First-party numbers from a single run on a 2019 laptop (the doc itself calls single-run output noisy and says the graphs use 16 repetitions, which are images not text). nlohmann version and compiler are not stated, so tier A is not met. Dart is not a parser: its finalized-parse figure is RapidJSON parsing plus lowering to the Dart buffer, so the large win over nlohmann mostly reflects RapidJSON versus nlohmann, and the project's own text says sajson is the choice for raw parse speed. The key-lookup row measures lookups in Dart's sorted flat buffer, not parse-time work. The repo's LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 although the list tag said MIT. The repo was archived by the owner on Jul 16, 2024 and the last commit is 2021-09-11.
